newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee again closes at new low vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee again closes at new low vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee ended at a new closing low of 57.10 against the dollar on Wednesday, the third consecutive day to hit a closing record, as banks rushed to cover short positions, dealers said.
"There was a lot of demand for dollars because of the year-end festival season," said a foreign bank dealer. "Supply was not enough. So people bought from the central bank."
The central bank's dollar selling rate was 57.1079 rupees, which was 3.5 local cents higher than yesterday.
The rupee closed at 57.05 on Tuesday, driven by a dearth of dollars caused by high oil prices.
Dealers said they expected the rupee to remain near the central bank's selling rate because of demand to cover imports in the run-up to the festival season.

"Some banks covered short positions at 57.11 without going to the central bank," said a local bank dealer. "Everybody expects the rupee to depreciate further so they are trading on the dollar at the higher level."
The overnight call money rate ended at 13.5 percent after opening at 15, with the market remaining liquid, dealers said. It closed at 14 percent on Tuesday.
